title: Preparation and Structural Evaluation of Epithelial Cell Monolayers in a Physiologically Sized Microfluidic Culture Device
protocol: Fabricate the microfluidic channel.
Separate the upper portion from the polycarbonate base plate.
Obtain a #1.5 rectangular coverglass with dimensions of 60 mm x 22 mm.
Clean surfaces of the coverglass in an ultrasonic bath.
Treat one side of the coverglass with a 0.1 mg/mL solution of Poly-D-Lysine at room temperature for 5 min.
Dry the treated coverglass at 60 °C for 30 min.
Affix a 0.13 mm thick double-sided adhesive to the flow array top, aligning the channel cut-outs precisely.
Affix a 0.1 mm thick mylar spacer to the adhesive strip, aligning the channel cut-outs precisely.
Repeat steps of affixing adhesive and spacers until desired channel height is achieved.
For example, for a channel height of 0.6 mm, use two spacers and three adhesive strips.
Affix a rectangular coverglass to the bottom-most adhesive strip with the Poly-D-Lysine-treated side facing the adhesive.
Apply firm and equal pressure to the top and bottom of construction and hold for 1 min.
Rinse the channel with de-ionized water using a syringe, simultaneously checking for leaks.
Sterilize channel enclosure in an ultraviolet (UV) sterilizer for 30 min.
Treat the channel with 2.0 µg/mL human fibronectin in phosphate buffered saline (PBS).
Incubate the treated channel for at least 30 min at 37 °C.

Use a micropipette to transfer an even suspension of NCI-H441 cells in RPMI 1640 medium with 10% fetal bovine serum to seed two microfluidic channels, each with cells at a surface density of 150,000 cells/cm2.
For 50 mm x 5 mm x 0.6 mm channels, use 0.25 mL of a 2.5 x 10^6 cells/mL suspension to fill each channel, as well as a portion of the ports.
Verify that cells have been distributed evenly within the channels using a brightfield microscope.
Culture the two channels for 24 h and 48 h respectively at 37 °C with 5% CO2 using a programmable syringe pump.
Draw spent media out from the channel and fresh media into the channel from a sterile media reservoir attached to channel inlet comprised of a cut-open 20 mL syringe covered with paraffin film.
Introduce and pump fresh media from the reservoir through the channel at a variable flow rate beginning at 0.2 µL/min and ramping up to 10 µL/min for 4 h, maintaining at that rate thereafter.
Prepare formaldehyde solutions by using 4% formaldehyde in PBS (methanol-free).
Dilute the first portion of formaldehyde solution to a concentration of 1% formaldehyde using Dulbecco's phosphate buffered saline (DPBS; with Ca2+ and Mg2+) as the diluent.
Dilute the second portion of formaldehyde solution to a concentration of 2% formaldehyde using DPBS as the diluent.
Transfer 4 mL of each diluted formaldehyde solution to separate 5 mL syringes and label accordingly.
Draw up 20 mL of DPBS into a separate 20 mL syringe.
Remove microfluidic channels from the culture apparatus.
Place the channels into the chemical fume hood.
Assemble the fixation and staining apparatus.
Attach a 10 cm segment of transfer tubing to the side port of a three-way stopcock via a male Luer lock to hose barb adapter.
Connect the stopcock to the inlet port of the flow array.
Attach another 10 cm segment of transfer tubing to the outlet port of the flow array using the same type of hose barb adapter.
Secure the free ends of both transfer tubes in a chemical and biohazard-appropriate waste container.
Turn the stopcock to block off the flow array inlet port.
Flush the waste line with DPBS.
Turn the stopcock to block off the waste line.
Slowly wash cells with 2 mL of DPBS.
Repeat the flushing step using the new solution every time.
Introduce a new solution (or concentration of solution) to the channel.
Slowly push 2 mL of 1% fixative solution through the channel.
Allow the 1% fixative solution to sit for 5 min.
Slowly push 2 mL of 2% fixative solution through the channel.
Allow the 2% fixative solution to sit for 15 min.
Wash cells by slowly introducing 2 mL of fresh DPBS to the channel in three separate instances (5 min each).
Complete steps 1.3.3-1.3.7 for both microfluidic channels in parallel.
Stain, permeabilize, and add mounting media to the cells in the microfluidic channel.
Prepare 0.1% saponin solution by adding 1 mg of saponin per mL of DPBS to produce 4 mL of solution.
Gently vortex the mixture to ensure thorough mixing.
Draw up 8 mL of DPBS into a 20 mL syringe.
Add two drops (0.1 mL) of F-actin-staining phalloidin reagent and two drops (0.1 mL) of nucleus-staining Hoechst reagent per mL of saponin solution to the mixture.
Cover the prepared staining/permeabilizing solution with aluminum foil to protect from light.
Flush the line with a small amount of staining/permeabilizing solution.
Introduce 2 mL of the staining/permeabilizing solution into the microfluidic channel and cover it with aluminum foil.
Allow the channel to sit at room temperature for 30 min.
Flush out the staining/permeabilizing solution twice with 2 mL of DPBS, allowing 5 mins per flush.
Add a suitable mounting media into the channel for better image quality.
Introduce a minimal amount of soft-set antifade mountant to each port of the microfluidic channel using a micropipette.
Ensure that the bottom surface is completely covered and no bubbles are trapped within the desired imaging area.
Seal the ends of the channel.
Verify cell layer integrity by observing under a brightfield microscope.
Complete steps 1.4.3-1.4.5 for both microfluidic channels in parallel.
Adjust confocal microscope settings including laser power, gain, offset, and scan parameters such as scan speed, scan area, scan format, resolution, and pinhole diameter.
Take reference scans and Z-stacks until desired image parameters and conditions are met.
Optimize imaging at sequentially higher-magnification objectives up to the 40x oil-immersion objective.

Construct Z-stacks at five locations on the flow array base plate: first electrode location, halfway between center and first electrode, center, halfway between center and last electrode, last electrode.
Perform image processing and data analysis.
Export XZ and YZ cross-sections using the confocal microscope software package.
Measure the total image area in pixels by using the Magic Wand tool outside of the image.
Measure the area excluding the total cross-sectional area of the cell layer in pixels by using the Magic Wand tool in the portion of the image exterior to the cell layer.
Subtract the exterior area pixel value from the total area pixel value to find the cross-sectional area pixel value.
Convert cross-sectional area pixel values to µm² values by multiplying pixel values by the square of the µm/pixel value.
Calculate means and standard deviations of data.
Graph results.
Treat the surface of culture wells with 2.0 μg/mL human fibronectin in PBS using sterile technique.
Incubate treated surfaces for at least 30 min at 37 °C.
Transfer 0.5 mL portions of NCI-H441 cell suspensions evenly into culture wells.
Verify even distribution of cells within the wells using a brightfield microscope.
Culture cells for 24 h, 48 h, and 96 h at 37 °C with 5% CO2.
Replace media daily during culturing period.
Prepare two portions of 4% formaldehyde in PBS.
Dilute one portion to a concentration of 1% formaldehyde using DPBS.
Dilute the other portion to 2% formaldehyde using DPBS.
Remove eight-well culture chambered coverglass from incubator.
Place the coverglass into the chemical fume hood.
Gently wash cells with 0.5 mL of DPBS using a micropipette.
Remove existing liquid from each well using a micropipette.
Introduce 0.5 mL of 1% fixative solution into each well and allow it to sit for 5 min.
Remove the 1% fixative solution from each well using the liquid-extraction method.
Introduce 0.5 mL of 2% fixative solution into each well and allow it to sit for 15 min.
Wash cells by introducing 0.5 mL of fresh DPBS into each well, allowing it to sit for 5 min, then remove the DPBS three times in total.
Prepare a 0.1% saponin solution by adding 1 mg of saponin per mL of DPBS and gently vortexing to mix.
To the 0.1% saponin solution, add two drops (0.1 mL) each of F-actin-staining phalloidin reagent and nucleus-staining Hoechst reagent per mL of saponin solution.
Cover the prepared staining/permeabilizing solution with aluminum foil to keep it away from light.
Introduce 0.2 mL of the staining/permeabilizing solution to each well, cover the chambered coverglass with aluminum foil, and allow it to sit at room temperature for 30 min.
Flush out the staining/permeabilizing solution twice with 0.5 mL of DPBS.
Add a suitable mounting media to the wells.
Introduce a minimal amount of soft-set antifade mountant into each well using a micropipette.
Verify cell layer integrity by observing under a brightfield microscope.
Adjust confocal microscope settings including laser power, gain, offset, and scan parameters.
Take reference scans and Z-stacks until desired image parameters are met.
Optimize imaging at sequentially higher-magnification objectives up to the 40x oil-immersion objective.
Construct Z-stacks of three random locations in each seeding density/culture duration match-up.
Export XZ and YZ cross sections using the confocal microscope software package.
Measure the total image area in pixels by using the Magic Wand tool outside of the image.
Measure the area excluding the total cross-sectional area of the cell layer in pixels by using the Magic Wand tool in the portion of the image exterior to the cell layer.
Subtract the exterior area pixel value from the total area pixel value to find the cross-sectional area pixel value using a data-processing software.
Convert cross-sectional area pixel values to µm² values by multiplying pixel values by the square of the µm/pixel value as indicated in the microscope software for the particular image.
Calculate means and standard deviations.
Graph results.
